s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic unilateral visual disturbance with signs of intraocular inflammation and macular edema
salient_findings: Blurry vision in one eye for several months
Cystoid macular edema with subfoveal fluid in the affected eye
Keratic precipitates and cells in the anterior chamber
key_facts: 65-year-old woman
Blurry vision in the right eye for several months
History of bilateral iritis
Amblyopia in the left eye
Bilateral posterior chamber intraocular lens
Left-sided mastectomy 2.5 years prior
On anastrozole therapy for more than 2 years
Visual acuity 20/25 OD and 20/150 OS
Normal intraocular pressures
Conjunctival injection and fine keratic precipitates in the right eye
Cystoid macular edema with a yellow spot in the fovea in the right eye
Epiretinal membrane in the left eye
No peripheral inflammation in either eye
Normal blood tests for vasculitis and rheumatologic disorders

shortlist.label: Cystoid Macular Edema secondary to Intraocular Lens
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has bilateral posterior chamber intraocular lens and presents with cystoid macular edema

shortlist.label: Uveitic Macular Edema
shortlist.why_kept: History of bilateral iritis and presence of fine keratic precipitates and cells in the anterior chamber

shortlist.label: Fuchs Heterochromic Iridocyclitis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic unilateral visual disturbance with signs of intraocular inflammation

shortlist.label: Anastrozole-induced Uveitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has been on anastrozole therapy for more than 2 years

shortlist.label: Intermediate Uveitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of fine keratic precipitates, cells in the anterior chamber, and cystoid macular edema

raw.rationale: The patient's history of recurrent bilateral iritis, presence of fine keratic precipitates, and cystoid macular edema are consistent with Fuchs Heterochromic Iridocyclitis. The condition is also characterized by chronic, low-grade inflammation, which aligns with the patient's presentation of trace conjunctival injection and cells in the anterior chamber.

rejected.label: Uveitis
rejected.why: Too broad, as uveitis is a general term that encompasses various forms of intraocular inflammation, including Fuchs Heterochromic Iridocyclitis

rejected.label: Herpes Simplex Iridocyclitis
rejected.why: Typically presents with more severe symptoms, such as pronounced pain, redness, and photophobia, which are not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Sympathetic Ophthalmia
rejected.why: Usually occurs after penetrating eye injury or surgery, which is not indicated in the patient's history, and typically presents with more severe and bilateral granulomatous uveitis

rejected.label: sarcoidosis
rejected.why: Would likely have other systemic manifestations and abnormal blood tests, which are not present in this case
